title: How Wireless Systems Actually Work: Introduction to the Series
summary: Discover the fundamental physical laws governing all wireless systems — bandwidth, noise, geometry, and energy. A seven-part engineering series by Anil Joseph, Senior Member IEEE, developing engineering judgment through first-principles thinking.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Emergency Locator Transmitters: When Reliability Means Survival
summary: How Cospas-Sarsat ELTs, EPIRBs, and PLBs use 406 MHz digital bursts, Doppler positioning, and satellite geometry to rescue survivors within hours — without GPS data from the beacon. From 121.5 MHz analog to Galileo Return Link Service.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Doppler, Time, and Geometry in RF: How Motion Encodes Information
summary: How Doppler shift, Time of Arrival (ToA), Time Difference of Arrival (TDoA), and geometric constraints enable positioning, velocity measurement, and signal detection. Unifying GNSS, radar, ADS-B multilateration, and search-and-rescue systems under one framework.
author: Anil Joseph

title: GNSS: Why Positioning Is Harder Than It Looks
summary: Why GPS accuracy depends on satellite geometry (GDOP), clock bias, ionospheric delay, multipath, and spoofing vulnerability — not just trilateration. A deep dive into why GNSS is a fragile inference problem that succeeds only when time, geometry, and signal environment align simultaneously.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Link Budgets in the Real World: Energy as the Fundamental Constraint
summary: Why wireless systems are energy-limited before they are algorithm-limited. Complete guide to RF link budgets: Eb/N0, thermal noise floor at -174 dBm/Hz, spread-spectrum processing gain, fading margins, and why GNSS works 20 dB below the noise floor.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Bursty vs Continuous Transmission: How Scheduling Energy Changes Everything
summary: Why ELTs transmit 0.5-second bursts every 50 seconds instead of continuously — and what this reveals about energy structuring in wireless systems. How duty cycle, peak SNR, and burst timing affect detectability, battery life, latency, and interference in IoT, radar, and satellite systems.
author: Anil Joseph

title: AI at the Physical Layer: Where Learning Helps and Where Physics Dominates
summary: Where machine learning genuinely improves wireless systems — channel estimation, hardware nonlinearity compensation, beamforming, interference detection — and where physics sets hard limits that no AI can bypass: Shannon capacity, thermal noise, geometric dilution, and link budgets.
author: Ansh Kumar & Anil Joseph

title: Antennas: Where Wireless Performance Is Actually Determined
summary: How antenna gain, radiation patterns, impedance matching, and efficiency determine real-world wireless performance. A practical guide for engineers selecting and deploying antennas in industrial IoT and M2M systems.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Logarithmic Thinking and the Decibel: From Sound to Satellites
summary: Master decibel (dB) calculations for RF link budgets, SNR, and dynamic range. Understand why 10 log vs 20 log, thermal noise floor at -174 dBm/Hz, receiver sensitivity, and how logarithmic thinking unifies acoustics, vibration analysis, and wireless engineering.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Shannon Capacity: The Absolute Limit of Communication
summary: Shannon's theorem C = B·log₂(1+SNR) defines the absolute limit of any wireless channel. Why infinite bandwidth cannot overcome finite energy, how Eb/N0 sets the -1.59 dB ultimate threshold, and how 5G LDPC and Turbo codes approach but never exceed this fundamental boundary.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Why Shorter Wavelength Does Not Always Mean Shorter Range
summary: Why shortwave (HF, 3-30 MHz) signals travel thousands of kilometres via ionospheric sky-wave while FM stays local. Understanding ground wave, ionospheric refraction, and why propagation mode — not wavelength — determines wireless range in MW, SW, and FM bands.
author: Anil Joseph

title: Reading the Indian Power Grid from the Streets: Seeing Engineering in Plain Sight
summary: Decode India's power grid from street level: insulator disc count reveals voltage (11kV to 765kV), conductor bundling controls corona discharge, Stockbridge dampers prevent fatigue failure, and corona rings shape electric fields. Every visible feature is a response to physics.
author: Anil Joseph

title: The Sun: Earth's External Power Supply
summary: Earth receives 1361 W/m² from the Sun — powering weather, photosynthesis, ocean currents, and civilization. A thermodynamic perspective on Earth's energy balance, why the temperature difference between Sun and space drives all life, and why fossil fuels are ancient stored sunlight.
author: Anil Joseph
